title: Strategy's Bitcoin Holdings Swing to $1.4 Billion Gain After Five-Day Rally
excerpt: The largest corporate Bitcoin holder flipped from a $13 billion unrealized loss to a gain as cryptocurrency surged 22% in five sessions.
body:
• Strategy's 840,447 BTC holdings swung from a $13 billion unrealized loss to a $1.4 billion gain as Bitcoin rallied to approximately $78,500
  • Bitcoin surged roughly 22% over five consecutive trading sessions, recovering from a 54% decline from its October 2025 peak of $126,000
  • Strategy built a $4.8 billion cash reserve and sold approximately 6,916 BTC during the downturn, providing 2.8 years of dividend coverage
  • The company has repurchased $347 million of its STRC preferred stock as part of a $1 billion buyback program

Strategy, the Nasdaq-listed company that has effectively transformed itself into a Bitcoin treasury vehicle, saw its cryptocurrency holdings swing to an unrealized gain of roughly $1.4 billion this week after a sharp rally lifted Bitcoin above the firm's average acquisition cost.

The company holds 840,447 BTC purchased at an average price of $75,385 per coin, according to CoinDesk. With Bitcoin trading at approximately $78,500, Strategy's position has moved decisively back into the black after months of paper losses that peaked near $13 billion when the cryptocurrency dropped to around $58,000 in July.

A Volatile Year for the Bitcoin Treasury Model

The turnaround came after Bitcoin surged approximately 22% over five consecutive trading sessions, its strongest sustained rally since late 2025. The cryptocurrency had fallen roughly 54% from its October peak of $126,000, dragging Strategy's balance sheet deep into unrealized loss territory.

The volatility has been punishing for Strategy shareholders. The stock fell 17% in a single session in February after reporting a $12.4 billion loss for the fourth quarter of 2025. In the first quarter of 2026, the company reported a $12.54 billion loss while continuing to buy Bitcoin, adding 89,599 BTC during the period.

"With more than 840,000 Bitcoin on its balance sheet, relatively modest changes in the cryptocurrency's market price can translate into multibillion-dollar swings in the company's unrealized gains and losses."

— CoinDesk analysis

Cash Reserves Provide a Cushion

During the extended downturn, Strategy took steps to shore up its financial position. The company sold approximately 6,916 BTC and increased its cash reserves to $4.8 billion, enough to cover roughly 2.8 years of dividend payments and other obligations on its preferred stock and debt.

Strategy has also been actively supporting its perpetual preferred stock, STRC, repurchasing approximately $347 million of the security over the past four weeks. That buyback consumed more than a third of the company's $1 billion authorized repurchase program, as management worked to push STRC back toward its $100 par value.

Analysts See Upside Despite Risks

Investment bank Canaccord recently raised its price target on MSTR to $224 from $185, reiterating a Buy rating. The firm pointed to the stock's 80% rebound since February and highlighted Strategy's preferred-share financing model as a key tool for raising capital without diluting common shareholders.

The company's BTC-per-share metric rose 18% year over year through the first quarter, suggesting that despite ongoing share issuance to fund Bitcoin purchases, each MSTR share represents a growing claim on the underlying cryptocurrency holdings.

Executive Chairman Michael Saylor has warned investors to prepare for "difficult years" ahead, but the company has shown no signs of pulling back from its core strategy. Strategy remains the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin globally, with a position that dwarfs those of other public companies in the space.

Whether the current rally marks the beginning of a sustained recovery or another leg in what has been an exceptionally volatile 2026 for cryptocurrency markets remains to be seen. For Strategy's shareholders, the answer will determine whether the company's all-in Bitcoin bet continues to pay off or reverts to the deep losses that characterized much of this year.
